name: Abu Qatifa al-Umawi
bio: Amr ibn al-Walid ibn Uqba was an Umayyad poet of Medina, known as Abu al-Walid and nicknamed Abu Qatifa. Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr exiled him to Syria with other Umayyads, and in his poems he asks after the palms of Medina, its paved quarter and the valley of al-Aqiq. Singers preserved some of his verse. His lines recalling a palace, palm trees and the ridge of al-Jamma' open the first poet’s account in Abu al-Faraj al-Isfahani’s Book of Songs. Abu al-Faraj relates that Ibn al-Zubayr granted him safe conduct and that he died on his way back to Medina, a death al-Zirikli dates to around 70 AH (690 CE).
